speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how does the job openings for fresh graduates in the third quarter of 2023 (3Q2023) compare against the same period in 2022; (b) what is the proportion of recently employed fresh graduates who secured (i) contractual and (ii) full-time roles; and (c) considering that the 3Q2023 Labour Market Advance Release reported a decline in the proportion of firms with an intention to hire due to worsened business expectations, what is the Government's assessment of the impact on fresh graduates.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is because employers do not usually specify the demographic requirements of job applicants in their job advertisements, as this is a breach of the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Based on the annual Graduate Employment Survey (GES), employment outcomes for fresh graduates from our autonomous universities, polytechnics and Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs) have remained strong.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Nadia also asked about the proportion of fresh graduates in contractual roles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Full-time permanent employment includes contracts lasting one year or more.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: While hiring sentiments have dipped in the third quarter of 2023, the overall labour market remains tight.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have been highlighting the downward trend in terms of the job vacancies because of the tougher, uncertain economic outlook that is facing us, with the economic headwinds in the next few quarters.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will continue to closely monitor the situation and we will stand ready to assist our graduates.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Fresh graduates can reach out to Education and Career Coaches in their respective Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) should they require support in their job search or tap on Workforce Singapore's (WSG) career matching services.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The first, whether there is any statistics on underemployment, in terms of whether the graduates going into these roles are facing that issue?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second, I know the Minister mentioned career counselling, WSG, and so on.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there any other more specific resources for fresh graduates that they may tap for upskilling in the interim, while looking for a job, because SkillsFuture may not be so applicable to the younger graduates?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, on underemployment, the measure that we have is time-related under-employment.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because of the tight labour market, time-related underemployment has been on a downward trend.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, of all employed residents in Singapore, time-related underemployment accounts for about 3% of the entire employed workforce for residents.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In terms of the programmes, we have quite an extensive range of programmes to support our fresh graduates.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At the IHLs, our students and graduates can tap on the Education and Career Counselling Services to find out more about jobs and what kind of opportunities and skill adjacencies they can have by upskilling.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Leading Government agencies are working with industry partners.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are also working with the Labour Movement and with the unions to facilitate the entry of polytechnic and ITE graduates into good jobs within key priority sectors with attractive starting wages and also meaningful career progression pathways.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is to drive the shift in hiring practices in the tech industry from one that is qualification-based to one that is skills-based.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, we have Education and Career coaches and the career-matching services that WSG continues to provide, which offers a very good supplement to the current Education and Career Guidance programme provided by MOE as well as the IHLs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There is an entire slew of programmes available today for them to tap on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Notwithstanding that, we anticipate this tightness to ease in terms of the labour situation because of the uncertainties that we are entering into over the next one to two quarters.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will not hesitate to step up, and step in, to help our graduates further, should the need arise.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There will be statistics to show that as well.
